record.paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
record.original_question: When releasing synthetic networked time-series data generated by GANs, what privacy definition should be used for a given data-sharing use case, given that different release scenarios may require different protection goals and threat models?

evidence.quote: A meta question, not unique to our work, is finding the right definition of privacy for each use case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the task of releasing synthetic networked time-series data, i.e., multi-dimensional time series records together with associated categorical/continuous metadata describing each entity (such as users, devices, or flows in a network), produced by a generative model (e.g., a generative adversarial network) trained on a sensitive dataset D. A "privacy definition" is a formal mathematical specification consisting of: (i) a threat model (the adversary's prior knowledge, auxiliary information, and computational power), (ii) a secret to be protected (e.g., membership of a record, the value of a specific attribute, presence of a temporal pattern, identity linkage across records), and (iii) a quantitative guarantee (e.g., an (ε, δ)-bound on a divergence between output distributions on neighboring datasets, a bound on an adversary's posterior advantage, or a bound on reconstruction error).

Formulate a principled framework that, given a data-sharing use case characterized by:
  - the structure of the data (per-entity time series plus metadata),
  - the intended downstream analytical tasks,
  - the assumed adversarial capabilities and auxiliary information, and
  - the utility requirements,
selects or constructs a privacy definition that is (a) semantically meaningful for the stated threat model, (b) composable under repeated releases, (c) achievable simultaneously with acceptable utility on the stated tasks, and (d) interpretable to data custodians.

Specifically: characterize, for the class of networked time-series release problems above, which privacy definitions (e.g., record-level differential privacy, user-/group-level differential privacy, Pufferfish privacy with appropriate secret/discriminative-pair structure, attribute privacy, membership-inference resistance, or task-specific indistinguishability notions) are appropriate for which use cases, and provide criteria under which one definition strictly dominates another for a given use case.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly framed as an open meta-question about choosing the right privacy definition per use case. The literature on differential privacy, Pufferfish privacy, and synthetic data continues to debate appropriate privacy notions for time-series and relational data, with no consensus framework. No source establishes a definitive resolution, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Pufferfish: A Framework for Mathematical Privacy Definitions
status_evidence.snippet: Pufferfish allows application domain experts to develop customized privacy definitions for their use cases.
status_evidence.claim: The choice of an appropriate privacy definition per use case is acknowledged as an unresolved design problem requiring custom frameworks.

status_evidence.title: SoK: Differential Privacies
status_evidence.snippet: We propose a systematization of knowledge of the many variants of differential privacy proposed in the literature, highlighting the lack of a single best definition.
status_evidence.claim: There is no single accepted privacy definition; selection depends on threat model and use case, indicating the question remains open.
